item.research_question: What are the synthetic strategies toward high entropy materials and how can they be used to achieve maximum disorder?
item.material_system: High entropy materials, including alloys, oxides, chalcogenides, and other multicomponent systems
item.processing_route: Atom-up synthetic approaches, including solvothermal synthesis, carbothermal shock synthesis, sol–gel synthesis, and molecular-precursor approaches
key_findings: High entropy materials can be synthesized using atom-up approaches, which allow for homogeneous mixing of elements at the atomic scale
Atom-up approaches can be used to synthesize a wide range of high entropy materials, including alloys, oxides, and chalcogenides
The molecular precursor approach is a versatile and scalable technique for synthesizing high entropy materials
High entropy materials can exhibit unique properties, such as entropy stabilization, sluggish diffusion, and the cocktail effect
The number of unique sites in a high entropy material can be extremely large, making it challenging to model and characterize these materials
item.mechanism: The authors propose that the high configurational entropy of high entropy materials can be achieved through the use of atom-up synthetic approaches, which allow for homogeneous mixing of elements at the atomic scale
item.limitations: The authors note that the synthesis of high entropy materials can be challenging, particularly when it comes to achieving homogeneous mixing of elements at the atomic scale
item.future_work: The authors propose the development of suitable modeling approaches as an important complementary research direction to synthesis and characterization protocols, and suggest the use of artificial intelligence for scaling atomistic simulations to more realistic supercells
quotes: High-entropy materials are a nascent class of materials that exploit a high configurational entropy to stabilize multiple elements in a single crystal lattice

The use of atom-up synthetic approaches to build crystal lattices atom by atom, rather than the top-down alteration of extant crystalline lattices, could lead to faster, lower-temperature, and more sustainable approaches to obtaining high entropy materials
The molecular precursor approach is ideally suited to the synthesis of high-entropy materials as it allows mixing, at the atomic level, of the precursors prior to synthesizing the HE lattice
